title: Xi Jinping Pushes China's Military to Accelerate AI and Unmanned Combat Systems
excerpt: Beijing is embedding artificial intelligence across its defence apparatus — from autonomous robot dogs to drone swarms — as the US-China military technology race intensifies.
body:
• Xi Jinping has directed China's military to accelerate development of AI-powered and unmanned combat technologies, framing them as central to "new quality combat capabilities," according to Bloomberg.
  • China's DeepSeek AI model is powering military applications including the Norinco P60 autonomous combat-support vehicle, with drone swarms and AI robot dogs also under development.
  • A DeepSeek-powered system reportedly assessed 10,000 battlefield scenarios in 48 seconds — a task that would take human military planners 48 hours, according to Reuters.
  • The US currently holds a "commanding" AI lead over China, with more than 4,000 data centres compared to roughly 400 in China, per a West Point study.

The Push for 'New Quality Combat Capabilities'

Chinese President Xi Jinping has ordered the People's Liberation Army to intensify its pursuit of artificial intelligence and unmanned combat technologies, according to Bloomberg. The directive frames AI-driven weapons systems as essential to what Beijing calls "new quality combat capabilities" — a concept that analysts say encompasses intelligent warfare, autonomous targeting, and unmanned operations across land, sea, and air.

The push builds on years of incremental investment. During China's top legislative meetings, Xi called on military delegates to "deepen reforms and promote innovation to enhance strategic capabilities in emerging areas," according to GlobalSecurity, citing reports from the PLA Daily.

DeepSeek Goes to War

A Reuters investigation published in October 2025 revealed the systematic scale of China's military AI integration. State-owned defence giant Norinco unveiled the P60, a military vehicle capable of autonomously conducting combat-support operations at 50 km/h, powered by DeepSeek — the AI model that became a source of national pride in China's tech sector.

https://x.com/Eng_china5/status/2083249047578751283

The PLA is also developing AI-powered robot dogs that scout in packs and drone swarms that autonomously track targets, according to procurement documents reviewed by Reuters. A November 2024 PLA tender called for AI-powered robot dogs that could scout for threats and clear explosive hazards.

"A DeepSeek-powered system was able to assess 10,000 battlefield scenarios — each with different variables, terrain, and force deployments — in 48 seconds. Such a task would have taken a conventional team of military planners 48 hours."

— Xi'an Technological University researchers, via Reuters

The US Advantage — For Now

Despite China's ambitions, the United States retains a significant lead. The Modern War Institute at West Point concluded in a March 2026 study that the US armed forces have a "commanding" AI advantage, pointing to America's 4,000-plus data centres compared to roughly 400 in China. Four-year-old US export controls on advanced semiconductors continue to constrain Beijing's access to AI-related hardware, according to Defense News.

PLA-linked Chinese universities, including institutions on the US Bureau of Industry and Security's Entity List, have been seeking access to Nvidia H200 chips — the most powerful AI processors permitted for sale in China — through procurement channels that may circumvent direct export controls, Bloomberg reported in June 2026.

India's Security Calculus

China's military AI buildup carries direct implications for India's defence posture along the contested Himalayan border and in the Indian Ocean. The PLA's pursuit of autonomous surveillance and rapid decision-making systems could alter the dynamics of border standoffs, where response times matter. India has been expanding its own defence technology investments, but the scale of China's state-directed integration of commercial AI into military platforms represents a different order of ambition.

For the Indian diaspora, the US-China military technology competition also shapes the geopolitical environment around India's semiconductor ambitions, defence procurement from the West, and the broader Indo-Pacific security architecture.

What to Watch

The effectiveness of US export controls on AI chips remains the key constraint on China's military AI timeline. Whether Beijing can develop domestic alternatives fast enough — and whether the PLA can move from procurement tenders to operational deployment — will determine how quickly the military balance shifts.
